about: A world has two physics at once. Looking travels: it reaches what a walk of shared lookings reaches and stops at the horizon.
A bound does not travel: it carries no step and no distance, and moving it changes cells past that horizon in one act.
Counting the bound as if it were a looking would make the whole world one neighbourhood, which is how the two are told apart.
The two physics side by side, in one world of a hundred cells. Looking is local: it reaches seventy-three cells, one step at a time, stops at the horizon, and moves a floor.

Signing is not: it reaches the sixty-six cells that rest on the bound, at no distance, past any horizon, and moves a ceiling. Seven of the cells it turned are cells no looking from the observer could have reached.

cases.name: seventy-three cells reached by looking, thirty-two changed by one signature
one world, two ways to change it
